scope: Ascend950PR BF16 RMSNorm, R1-R84, two sessions

eras.B: R59-R80 L2 policy + exhaustive negative results

ledger.topic: SimdVF reduction and bf16 load resolved by probe
ledger.outcome: vcadd reduction chain and bf16 UNPK_B16 load verified equal to torch; SimdVF route declared viable

ledger.topic: bf16 store, scalar broadcast, rstd chain
ledger.outcome: all SimdVF API pieces needed by RMSNorm verified individually; no full kernel or timing yet

ledger.topic: first end-to-end SimdVF RMSNorm kernel
ledger.outcome: correct SimdVF kernel exists and beats the SimtVF one, but is ~0.58x of vendor; w preconversion 0.539->0.581x

ledger.topic: pipe attribution, bf16 vector width, rows sweep
ledger.outcome: vector-pipe floor identified; rows 1->4 gives real 1.76x but rows=8 does not fit UB

ledger.topic: decode shape faster than vendor; cube path blocked
ledger.outcome: decode >1.0 in single-process paired measurement; prefill ~0.62x; nothing witness-audited yet

ledger.topic: why prefill cannot reach parity (op-count accounting)
ledger.outcome: ~10 vector instructions per 64 elements with no available fusion primitive; concluded scheduling alone cannot close it

ledger.topic: kernel iterations v2-v3, structural tuning, pipeline depth, multi-accumulator
ledger.outcome: v3/v4 candidates built; decode progressed; prefill remained ~0.70-0.76; no candidate certified
ledger.note: log-only summary; per-round detail not separately archived

ledger.topic: multi-accumulator candidate; certification structurally blocked
ledger.outcome: R47 multi-accumulator candidate could not be certified because own ForgeKernel runs occupied the card

ledger.topic: independent acceptance in a genuinely clean window
ledger.outcome: decode demonstrated faster than vendor under audited protocol; prefill ~0.757 and fails

ledger.topic: prefill gap analysis: where the remaining 32% sits
ledger.outcome: no prefill improvement established; ad-hoc sweeps cannot resolve the gap

ledger.topic: deeper pipeline + double-buffered output
ledger.outcome: structural tuning does not move the gated prefill ratio (~0.75); decode EXCEED stands

ledger.topic: v4 certified EXCEED on decode (single artifact)
ledger.outcome: decode certified EXCEED 1.2809 [1.2470,1.3087]; prefill 0.757 fails; partition hypothesis untested

ledger.topic: UB limit is enforced at launch; unlimit annotation does not help
ledger.outcome: annotate_unlimit_memory does not change the launch-time UB check (286720 B always refused)

ledger.topic: gate can report authenticity FAIL when candidate measured nothing
ledger.outcome: gate bug: no measurement and no observed kernel was judged 'delegates to vendor'; fixed to RETEST

ledger.topic: claimed contiguous-partition gain (+8.9%)
ledger.outcome: claimed prefill 0.757->0.825 from contiguous per-core partition

withdrawn.reason: candidate ms only moved 0.0801->0.0794 (~0.8%, noise); the ratio moved because the VENDOR window drifted 0.0591->0.0645. Claim retracted.

ledger.topic: environment saturated by other users
ledger.outcome: nothing new measured; variants queued behind idle-window waits

ledger.topic: v5 precision coverage across input families
ledger.outcome: precision clean on both shapes and all tested families; performance still short on prefill

ledger.topic: CORRECTION: partition change never improved the candidate
ledger.outcome: R54 claim withdrawn; established the rule that CANDIDATE time is the metric, not the ratio alone

ledger.topic: two-phase scheduling is unsafe: a genuine race
ledger.outcome: two-phase shared-buffer kernel has a REAL race: rows=2 wrong at all sizes, batch=128 nondeterministic (5 runs differ, rel=1.0). v10/v11/v13/v14/v14b REJECTED; their 0.0733 ms is not a performance result.

ledger.topic: race-free two-phase via source-level unroll with per-row registers
ledger.outcome: v15 correct and deterministic at all sizes; gated prefill 0.0794->0.0755 ms, first confirmation the two-phase approach works

ledger.topic: compute has caught up; the bottleneck moved to DMA
ledger.outcome: vec 41.0 us vs vendor 37.2 us; deeper buffering does not help; parity would need ~30% off candidate at vendor-best

ledger.topic: v16 single artifact: decode EXCEED, prefill short
ledger.outcome: v16 certified decode 1.3160x

ledger.topic: copy-path floor explains the remaining prefill gap
ledger.outcome: measured copy path ~1.7 TB/s; pure copy of 128 MB needs 0.078 ms; concluded the path had bottomed out

withdrawn.reason: WRONG. The path was not saturated but crippled by an UNSET L2 write policy; an explicit policy lifted write throughput 1.13->3.08 TB/s and the candidate to 0.0648 ms.

ledger.topic: L2 cache policy is the decisive knob
ledger.outcome: explicit write-path NORMAL_FV lifts UB->GM from 1.13 to 3.08 TB/s (2.7x); read peaks 2.35 TB/s; v18 candidate 0.0648 ms, best so far. R64's floor claim withdrawn.

ledger.topic: microbenchmark ranking does not transfer to the kernel
ledger.outcome: NORMAL_LV won the read microbenchmark but made the kernel SLOWER; v21 adopted NORMAL_FV on every DMA path

ledger.topic: v23 is the best artifact on both shapes
ledger.outcome: v23 (stages=4 + NORMAL_FV everywhere) decode 1.3726 [1.3561,1.3829]; prefill 0.8074 [0.8006,0.8343] FAIL; more output buffering hurts

ledger.topic: systematic negation of the remaining lever space
ledger.outcome: rows=2, rows=8, stages=5/6, 8 accumulation chains, y triple-buffering, heterogeneous read/write L2 policies, manual pipeline order/stage lists: NONE beats v23

ledger.topic: v23 precision across four input families on both shapes
ledger.outcome: precision pass; decode 1.3726/1.4056; prefill 0.807/0.813

ledger.topic: archive reproduces from a fresh empty cache
ledger.outcome: decode reproduces 1.3550x from a cold cache; bigger DMA chunks useless once L2 policy is set (32 KB=1.757 TB/s, 64 KB=1.725 TB/s)

ledger.topic: residual gap is MIXED-traffic efficiency
ledger.outcome: isolated read 2.35 / write 3.08 TB/s but mixed only 1.76; our kernel 1.97 vs vendor 2.42 TB/s, matching the ~20% time gap. TileLang exposes no DRAM page-locality or stream-count control.

ledger.topic: CORRECTION: for prefill the RATIO is the stable quantity
ledger.outcome: absolute prefill times drift +/-20% between windows; only the paired ratio is stable (0.771-0.813). Sharpened the rule: a single-window improvement under 20% is not evidence.

ledger.topic: documentation-to-evidence audit
ledger.outcome: 5 documentation numbers audited against raw evidence, all exactly consistent; manifest hashes regenerated

ledger.topic: fourth independent prefill window: best ratio still 0.85
ledger.outcome: fourth clean window gives 0.8502 [0.8294,0.8830] - the best of four and still FAIL

ledger.topic: pre-delivery verification in a fresh process
ledger.outcome: shipped v23 reproduces correctly and deterministically; objective not achieved

ledger.topic: closing record at the round budget (80/80)
ledger.outcome: decode EXCEED on 3 windows; prefill FAIL on 4 windows (0.771-0.850); objective_met=false; lever list declared exhausted

withdrawn.reason: Declared the lever space exhausted, but had never varied the grid size (all candidates used 64 blocks on a 56-core chip) nor tested the read-path NOTALLOC_CLEAN policy. Both were reachable at any time.

ledger.topic: msprof op simulator feasibility on a minimal v23 model
ledger.outcome: simulator exists and runs; usable as a model, trustworthiness of per-pipe numbers unestablished

ledger.topic: SIMT-looking mnemonics are the model naming convention
ledger.outcome: corrected the earlier misreading that SIMT_LDK/SIMT_STG/SIMT_FFMA implied a compiler fallback to a SIMT path

ledger.topic: simulator cannot discriminate 12% kernel differences
ledger.outcome: v23 vs v28 are BIT-IDENTICAL in simulation (total_tick 43686 vs 43804; both 338639 cycles, 13925 executed) while differing 12% on hardware. No offline oracle is available; only the device can settle a 12% question.

ledger.topic: 56 blocks (not 64) + NOTALLOC_CLEAN read path
ledger.outcome: Two independent host-side changes flip prefill from FAIL to EXCEED. (1) grid 64 -> 56: the chip has 56 AIV cores, so 64 blocks costs a second near-empty wave. (2) read path NORMAL_FV -> NOTALLOC_CLEAN: our 128 MB footprint exactly fills the 128 MB L2, so the allocating read policy forced dirty-Y write-backs into the read stream. Kernel body is byte-identical to v23.

note: Era boundary note: R79/R80 are the closing of the Era-B program and are grouped with it; Era C begins at R81 in the current session. Dates for R81-R83 were corrected from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-03 to match their artifacts.
